page: Amazon Web Services r7i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It operates on the x86_64 architecture using custom Intel Xeon 8488C processors clocked at 3.2 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced hardware instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), enabling hardware-level acceleration for matrix and vector operations without dedicated accelerator cards.

Memory capacity is a core focus of the r7i.8xlarge, providing 256 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 5 GHz. This yields an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. In synthetic and realistic benchmarks, this memory subsystem demonstrates strong large-block write bandwidth reaching 93.43 GB/sec. Compute evaluation shows strong single-core results, including a 2010.0 Geekbench single-core score and fast single-threaded gzip compression at 31.9 GB/sec. Lightweight AI workloads show high throughput, clocking 390.06 tokens per second during small 135M-model text generation. Conversely, scaling to 70B parameter models reveals lower generation throughput due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage, meaning all persistent and scratch filesystem requirements rely on network-attached storage over the network plane. Baseline network throughput is rated at 12 Gbps, while zero integrated GPUs are bundled. From an operational efficiency perspective, the r7i.8xlarge delivers dense DDR5 capacity alongside dedicated compute threads, avoiding hypervisor oversubscription penalties. This server type is targeted at in-memory caching solutions like Redis, large enterprise relational database instances, memory-bound ETL workflows, and static web serving workloads requiring significant memory resident tables.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, delivering balanced compute and extensive memory density. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processors running at 3.2 GHz, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX acceleration extensions. It includes 256 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation that excels in memory-intensive processing and high-throughput static web serving. The configuration contains no local storage and does not include hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reflect top-tier performance for smaller-scale language model inference and strong single-core throughput alongside solid multi-threaded results. This hardware profile suits enterprise relational databases, large Redis caches, memory-bound analytics pipelines, and data-intensive backends.
